question: Which skin layer is primarily responsible for providing tensile strength and elasticity due to its rich content of collagen and elastin fibers?
explanation: The dermis is a dense fibrous connective tissue layer packed with collagen and elastin, giving skin its structural strength and resilience. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T7#GNS213_U5_T7_h1)

question: What is the primary structural role of lipids within the stratum corneum of the epidermis?

options.A: To act as a matrix preventing excessive water loss and pathogen entry
options.B: To supply continuous blood flow to the avascular epidermal cells
options.C: To produce melanin for protection against ultraviolet radiation
options.D: To anchor keratinocytes to the underlying basement membrane

explanation: Intercellular lipids in the stratum corneum form a hydrophobic barrier that stops transepidermal water loss and blocks external chemical or microbial irritants. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T7#GNS213_U5_T7_h1)

question: Which cellular component of the dermis rapidly releases preformed histamine and vasoactive amines upon activation?
explanation: Mast cells contain cytoplasmic granules filled with histamine and other inflammatory mediators that drive acute vasodilation and local swelling. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T7#GNS213_U5_T7_h2)

question: How do keratinocytes contribute directly to the early stages of skin inflammation?

options.A: By phagocytosing invading bacteria within the dermal matrix
options.B: By producing melanin to shield underlying vascular beds
options.C: By secreting pro-inflammatory cytokines like interleukin-1
options.D: By synthesizing structural collagen fibers to close open wounds

explanation: Stressed or damaged keratinocytes actively signal neighboring cells by releasing cytokines such as IL-1 and TNF-alpha, triggering the local immune response. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T7#GNS213_U5_T7_h2)

question: What distinguishes a patch from a macule?

options.A: A patch is larger than 1 cm in diameter, whereas a macule is smaller.
options.B: A patch contains purulent exudate, whereas a macule contains serous fluid.
options.C: A patch is fluid-filled, whereas a macule is solid.
options.D: A patch is elevated above the skin surface, whereas a macule is flat.

explanation: Both macules and patches are flat, non-elevated color changes, but a patch is defined by a larger surface area exceeding 1 centimeter. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T7#GNS213_U5_T7_h3)

question: A patient presents with a large, fluid-filled blister measuring 3 cm across on the trunk, caused by subepidermal cleavage. Which term accurately describes this primary lesion?
explanation: A fluid-filled elevated lesion exceeding 1 cm in diameter is classified as a bulla, whereas smaller versions are termed vesicles. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T7#GNS213_U5_T7_h3)

question: Which specific type of nerve fiber is primarily responsible for transmitting the sensation of pruritus from the skin to the central nervous system?
explanation: Slow-conducting, unmyelinated type C nerve fibers terminate in the skin and transmit itch and thermal sensations to the spinal cord. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T7#GNS213_U5_T7_h4)

question: Why does physical scratching provide temporary relief from an intense itch despite potentially worsening the underlying skin condition?

options.A: Friction removes the superficial stratum corneum to eliminate trapped histamine molecules.
options.B: Scratching permanently destroys local C-nerve endings in the affected tissue.
options.C: Mechanical pressure triggers an immediate release of anti-inflammatory cytokines from local mast cells.
options.D: Scratching stimulates mechanoreceptive fibers that gate-control and block itch signals at the spinal level.

explanation: Activating mechanoreceptors through scratching sends competing signals along larger fibers that inhibit itch transmission through spinal gate control, though this relief is short-lived. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T7#GNS213_U5_T7_h4)

question: What is the primary mechanism by which dermatophyte fungi colonize and damage the skin?

options.A: By secreting keratinases to break down the stratum corneum for nutrients
options.B: By releasing neurotoxins that paralyze local sweat gland secretion
options.C: By inducing systemic autoimmune responses against dermal collagen
options.D: By burrowing deep into the subcutaneous adipose tissue to reproduce

explanation: Dermatophytes rely on enzymes called keratinases to digest and utilize keratin proteins found in the stratum corneum, hair, and nails. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T7#GNS213_U5_T7_h5)

question: What is the underlying cause of the intense, delayed hypersensitivity-driven rash and itching experienced by patients with scabies infestations?

options.A: Immune reaction against mite feces and saliva deposited within the stratum corneum burrows
options.B: Mechanical destruction of large nerve bundles by mites tunneling through the dermis
options.C: Direct bacterial superinfection of deep dermal ulcerations caused by mite bites
options.D: Systemic toxicity resulting from the digestion of subcutaneous blood vessels by adult mites

explanation: The symptoms of scabies are largely driven by an allergic, delayed-type hypersensitivity reaction mounted by the host against the proteins and waste products left by the burrowing mites. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T7#GNS213_U5_T7_h5)

question: Which cytokine pathway plays a central role in driving the rapid keratinocyte proliferation seen in psoriatic plaques?
explanation: IL-17 produced by activated T cells is a key driver of the hyperproliferation and abnormal differentiation of keratinocytes in psoriasis. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T7#GNS213_U5_T7_h6)

question: How does filaggrin deficiency contribute to the pathophysiology of atopic dermatitis?

options.A: It accelerates the production of melanin, causing widespread hyperpigmentation.
options.B: It triggers immediate destruction of dermal collagen by matrix metalloproteinases.
options.C: It compromises epidermal barrier integrity, allowing allergens to penetrate and provoke immune responses.
options.D: It blocks the transmission of itch signals along unmyelinated C-fibers.

explanation: Filaggrin is an essential structural protein that aggregates keratin filaments to form a compact stratum corneum; its deficiency leads to a leaky skin barrier and chronic eczema. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T7#GNS213_U5_T7_h6)

question: During which phase of cutaneous wound healing do fibroblasts primarily migrate into the wound bed to deposit new collagen and extracellular matrix?
explanation: The proliferative phase is characterized by angiogenesis, granulation tissue formation, and active collagen deposition by fibroblasts to fill the wound defect. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T7#GNS213_U5_T7_h7)

question: Which clinical feature distinguishes a keloid scar from a hypertrophic scar?

options.A: A keloid typically resolves spontaneously without surgical or medical intervention.
options.B: A keloid remains strictly confined within the original margins of the skin injury.
options.C: A keloid extends and grows beyond the original boundaries of the wound.
options.D: A keloid consists primarily of type III collagen rather than type I collagen.

explanation: Keloids are characterized by aggressive, tumor-like fibrous growth that invades beyond the borders of the initial trauma, unlike hypertrophic scars which stay within the original wound margins. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T7#GNS213_U5_T7_h7)
